session.generation: The coordinator draws 32 bytes from a cryptographically secure random generator and lowercase-hex encodes them.
session.freshness: The coordinator must not reuse an identifier from any attempted or completed exchange. Each peer rejects an envelope whose identifier differs from the current exchange.
session.transport: GitHub Actions artifacts from two manually dispatched runs of pq-sequoia-macos.yml
session.execution_attempts: The qualification and response jobs accept only workflow run attempt 1. A failed job ends the exchange; restart with a fresh session identifier and new workflow runs instead of rerunning either job.
session.lifecycle: The macOS secret certificate exists only in the original running macOS job. The peer response must arrive before that job exits; no later job may resume decryption. Hatchery retains its opening secret through phase C signing, removes it before releasing the already signed phase C bytes, and releases nothing if cleanup fails.

detached_signatures.issuer: the exact signing subkey fingerprint in the accompanying inspected certificate

cryptographic_shape.receiver_rule: Inspect and enforce this shape before accepting a message signature, a transcript signature, or encrypting to the certificate. Verification success alone is insufficient.

authenticated_transcript.canonicalization: Remove control_signature from the complete envelope object, then serialize the remaining JSON recursively with object keys sorted by Unicode code point, ensure_ascii=true, separators ',' and ':', UTF-8 encoding, and no terminal newline.
authenticated_transcript.signature: control_signature is a detached version-6 ML-DSA-65+Ed25519 signature over the canonical bytes, issued by the exact signing subkey of that phase producer's disposable public certificate.
authenticated_transcript.continuity: Phase A uses 64 zeroes as parent_envelope_sha256. Phase B names the SHA-256 of the exact received phase-A envelope bytes. Phase C names the SHA-256 of the exact received phase-B envelope bytes and verifies under the same Hatchery certificate authenticated in phase A.
authenticated_transcript.closure_binding: For macos-ci-phase-b, producer_closure_sha256 is the SHA-256 of the exact sibling runtime-closure.json bytes emitted by record-runtime after the tap, sq and sqv bottle archives, and runtime are fixed. The coordinator reviews that sibling artifact and supplies its digest to the #148 receiver as the independent expected macOS closure; the envelope never establishes its own expected closure. Hatchery phases use the separately reviewed Hatchery closure digest supplied by the coordinator.
authenticated_transcript.protocol_binding: protocol_sha256 is the SHA-256 of this exact file. The maintained validator embeds and enforces it.

operations: generate and inspect one disposable certificate with the exact cryptographic shape
sign message.bin and inspect the exact signature algorithm and issuer
exercise certificate and signing and encryption subkey revocation against local copies
sign the canonical phase-A transcript with the same disposable signing key

secret_lifetime.cleanup_after: phase C is signed and before phase C is released

operations: enforce the phase-A transcript signature, parent, protocol, Hatchery closure, certificate shape, and message-signature issuer and algorithm
verify the Hatchery message signature and reject a locally altered message
generate and inspect one disposable certificate with the exact cryptographic shape
sign message.bin, encrypt it to the inspected Hatchery certificate, and exercise local revocations
record the complete runtime closure, including the exact sq and sqv bottle identities, ephemeral tap commit, and live dyld shared-cache membership evidence
set the signed producer closure to the SHA-256 of the exact retained runtime-closure.json bytes
sign and publish the parent-chained canonical phase-B transcript
wait for one exact response run bound to this qualifier run, phase-B digest, and reviewed commit

secret_lifetime.location: one GitHub-hosted macOS runner temporary directory
secret_lifetime.cleanup_after: macos-ci-close succeeds or the job exits

operations: require the sibling runtime-closure.json SHA-256 to equal the coordinator-supplied expected macOS closure digest and phase B's signed producer closure, then enforce the transcript signature, parent, protocol, certificate shape, and message-signature issuer and algorithm
verify the macOS message signature, reject an altered message, decrypt and tamper-test ciphertext-to-hatchery.pgp
encrypt message.bin to the inspected macOS certificate
create results/hatchery.json with the complete seven-artifact reciprocal digest map
sign the parent-chained canonical phase-C transcript with the retained opening signing key
remove all Hatchery disposable secret material before releasing the unchanged signed phase-C bytes

inputs: the still-running macOS job's local secret
operations: enforce the phase-C signature under the phase-A certificate and the exact phase-B parent digest
validate and retain results/hatchery.json and require its complete artifact map to equal macOS observations
decrypt and byte-compare ciphertext-to-macos-ci.pgp and reject its tampered copy without output
retain exact relay-run metadata and write results/macos-ci.json with the same complete artifact map
remove all runner-local secret and plaintext derivatives before serializing cleanup_complete=true

envelopes.bounds: Envelope and decoded payload sizes are checked before cryptographic use. Payload and result maps are closed; extra fields are rejected.

reciprocal_artifact_map.rule: The seven finite cryptographic transfer artifacts are the complete reciprocal map. Both peers can observe all seven before phase C. Transport envelopes, result JSON files, and SHA256SUMS are indexed separately because including a container's own digest inside itself is impossible. macOS rejects any missing, extra, or unequal Hatchery record.

relay_binding.selection: The relay run title contains the exact session ID, qualifier run ID, and phase-B envelope digest. The qualifier completes a workflow-scoped paginated traversal without named search filters, applies the attempt, event, commit, title, and state checks locally, rejects more than one distinct exact title match or an exact-title response with run_attempt greater than 1, waits until the sole first-attempt match is completed successfully, then validates its exact database ID, run attempt, event, status, conclusion, and head SHA against the reviewed qualifier commit before download.
relay_binding.final_check: Immediately after closing the live exchange and before final evidence indexing, the qualifier repeats the same complete traversal and requires the sole exact title match to be the selected successful first-attempt run.
relay_binding.duplicate_rule: Any second exact title match observed at either check rejects the session, including a queued, pending, in-progress, completed unsuccessful, or completed successful run.
relay_binding.rerun_rule: Any exact-title matching response whose run_attempt is greater than 1 rejects the session at either observation. Identical repeated provider records for the same database ID and run attempt are pagination overlap, while different attempts of one database ID remain distinct observations.

observation_coverage.pagination: gh api --paginate must reach a successful end before an observation is accepted.
observation_coverage.failure: A provider or CLI error, timeout, interruption, malformed page, malformed run, conflicting observation for one database ID and run attempt, or incomplete traversal rejects without producing an observation. A completed traversal with multiple distinct exact-title runs or an exact-title response at run_attempt greater than 1 writes a rejected observation before returning nonzero. No page or record cutoff is accepted.

relay_binding.retention: Each retained observation records its stage, exact exchange binding, selected run ID, successful pagination completion, endpoint, page size, page and record counts, repeated-record count, absence of named search filters, and every distinct exact-title run attempt. Identical repeats of one database ID and run attempt count once; a different attempt remains distinct, and conflicting values for one database ID and attempt reject. The validated first-attempt relay metadata remains copied into results/macos-ci.json.

rejected_observations.retention: After a complete selection or final traversal observes multiple distinct exact-title runs or an exact-title response at run_attempt greater than 1, the command writes the value-free record with no selected run and an explicit rejected outcome and reason, then returns nonzero. A selection rejection retains that record. A final rejection retains the already validated selection record and the rejected final record together. The failure-only artifact accepts only those two fixed paths; the normal qualification artifact remains success-only, and private, downloaded, and secret-bearing state is excluded.

relay_binding.temporal_limit: Submissions after the final check are outside the guarantee. The two complete provider traversals are not a permanent or global uniqueness guarantee, do not form an atomic provider snapshot, and make no claim about runs the provider does not return.

phase_b_closure_artifact.rule: The phase-B GitHub Actions artifact retains both exact files as siblings. The coordinator reviews runtime-closure.json and gives #148 its independently established SHA-256. #148 requires that digest to match both the received closure bytes and phase B's signed producer_closure_sha256 before using the macOS certificate or ciphertext.
phase_b_closure_artifact.non_circularity: runtime-closure.json does not contain its own digest. Its digest is carried by the separately signed phase-B envelope and later peer results; envelope, result, and final index digests remain outside the seven-artifact reciprocal cryptographic map.

artifact_policy.revocation_transfer_decision: Do not transfer revocation packets. Each peer exercises emergency certificate, explicit retired certificate, retired signing-subkey, and retired encryption-subkey transitions locally; only value-free result classifications, packet SHA-256 values, sizes, and scrubbed diagnostics enter result JSON.

macho_closure.hashed: Every resolved executable and dylib in the recursive closure, including Homebrew and candidate-keg objects.
macho_closure.run_path_resolution: Resolve each LC_RPATH in the image that defines it. For an @rpath install name, search the current image's entries in load-command order, then inherited entries from the nearest defining image outward. Keep @executable_path rooted at the root executable. Reject any path form that cannot be modeled exactly.
macho_closure.apple_shared_cache_membership: Run /usr/bin/dyld_shared_cache_util -list against the live cache. An unresolved install name is accepted only by exact membership in that successful nonempty listing. Retain the utility path, realpath, size, SHA-256, exact command, listing size and SHA-256, listed-name count, and the exact names used by each closure.
macho_closure.failure: Any unresolved dependency absent from the live shared-cache listing rejects closure recording. Pathname prefixes, including /usr/lib and /System/Library, never establish membership.

runtime_bottles.binding: record-runtime requires each exact same-job bottle archive and its brew bottle --json record before phase B fixes the runtime closure digest.
runtime_bottles.validation: The closed sq and sqv map must match candidate.json's formula and version, the arm64_sequoia tag, the ephemeral tap commit, the metadata local filename, and the archive SHA-256. The closure retains each metadata record's path, byte count, and SHA-256 and each archive's path, byte count, and SHA-256.
runtime_bottles.failure: Missing, extra, ambiguous, malformed, or mismatched metadata or archive inputs reject runtime-closure creation.

ephemeral_tap_closure.pre_build: prepare-tap copies both frozen formulae into the qualification tap and creates a local unsigned Git commit before either Homebrew build starts.
ephemeral_tap_closure.control: The tap index and worktree must be clean. Both the committed blob and working-tree bytes must exactly equal the formula bytes and SHA-256 frozen in candidate.json. record-runtime repeats this check after the build and embeds the result.

failure_semantics.identity_digest_signature_or_shape_misma: reject the session before using an unqualified shared command path
failure_semantics.workflow_rerun: reject a non-first qualification or response attempt before exchange input use; restart with a fresh session identifier and new workflow runs
failure_semantics.relay_timeout_or_ambiguity: reject and clean both local secret workspaces; never resume with a new macOS job
failure_semantics.operation_failure: retain only value-free failure classification and scrubbed diagnostics, then clean local secret material
failure_semantics.rollback: disable the candidate workflow; there is no accepted earlier macOS CI closure

required_observations: both peers enforce the exact RFC 9980 certificate and signature shape
all three canonical phase transcripts verify with exact closure, protocol, session, phase, parent, message, payload, and result bindings
phase C proves continuity with the Hatchery signing key authenticated in phase A
phase B's signed producer closure equals the exact reviewed runtime-closure.json bytes, including the sq and sqv bottle identities, tap commit, and live shared-cache observations
both peers verify the other's detached signature with exact sqv
both peers reject tampered ciphertext with no recovered output
both peers exercise certificate and subkey revocation locally
both peers report the same complete seven-artifact digest map
both peers report local secret cleanup complete
the final evidence retains one exact first-attempt relay run bound to the reviewed commit
